source_anchors.operation: parseFooter_ appends to the offset vectors and emplaces native ids without clearing, so a repeated openFile accumulates; first entry wins for a duplicate native id
spectra_before_chroms_ defaults to true and is only computed when both index sections are populated
copy constructor reopens the file but omits spectra_native_ids_ and chromatograms_native_ids_ from its initialiser list
chromatogram out-of-range message names spectra and reports getNrSpectra() as the maximum
last chromatogram ends at the first spectrum when chromatograms precede spectra, otherwise at index_offset_
readl = endidx - startidx handed to new char[] with no ordering, file-length or size check, and the stream read result is never inspected
last spectrum ends at the first chromatogram when spectra precede chromatograms, otherwise at index_offset_
getMSSpectrumById calls updateRanges once; getMSChromatogramById(int) at line 282 calls it a second time after the two-argument overload already did
XercesDOMParser parses the record text with no error handler installed, so the well-formedness errors caused by the trailing list and run tags in the last record's byte range are discarded
domParseString_ reads only defaultArrayLength, id and the binaryDataArray elements; every other record field is left default-constructed
PeakFileOptions RT, MS-level and precursor-m/z checks run before peak I/O and return a metadata-only spectrum; m/z and intensity ranges select peaks afterwards

evidence: Tier 3 source review. Every expected value is either a literal transcribed from IndexedMzMLFile_test.cpp and its unmodified fixture (2 spectra, 1 chromatogram, index offset 667742, record offsets 24146/345745/665563, native ids 'controllerType=0 controllerNumber=1 scan=1', '...scan=2', 'TIC', 19914/19800/48 points, ms level 1, scan start times 0.2961 s and 0.4738 s), or a self-consistency comparison against this crate's own whole-file mzML reader on the same fixture, which is what the class test does with MzMLFile().load. The offset-ordering branch, the hostile-index rejections and the PeakFileOptions behaviour use independently constructed documents (tier 4) because the upstream fixture cannot reach them. No C++ was built or executed and no C++ output was retained, so this is not a tier 1 differential.
gaps: The source parallelises nothing in this class, but its own class documentation recommends copying the handler for OpenMP use; this port is serial and offers no copy, so a second reader is a second open of the same path.
The Interfaces::Spectrum / Interfaces::Chromatogram pointer overloads are not ported; the crate has no OpenSWATH Interfaces layer.
setSkipXMLChecks is not ported: the crate's mzML reader has no unchecked fast path.
